assumptions: Time window is 22 Oct to 31 Oct 2026, as stated explicitly in the question.
A risk decline means failure_category = risk_decline, which includes ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE, RISK_RULE_DECLINE and SUSPECTED_FRAUD.
caveats: Attempt volume in 22–31 Oct was 39% above the usual level for those weekdays. This can be a real business event such as a sale or a data gap; it is not a data error by itself, but check before comparing totals across this period.
Failure rates shown are each BIN's risk declines as a share of its own attempts, not of all attempts, so a BIN with high volume can rank high on counts without having a high rate.

facts.text: There were 2,516 risk-decline failed card attempts between 22 and 31 October 2026.
BIN 911001 (Harbor Bank) had the most risk declines: 371, or 14.7% of the total (14.75% in the evidence). Its risk-decline rate was 15.7% of its 2,360 attempts.
BIN 911003 (Harbor Bank) was second with 345 risk declines (13.7% of the total), a 15.3% risk-decline rate on 2,255 attempts.
BIN 911002 (Harbor Bank) was third with 297 risk declines (11.8% of the total), a 13.3% risk-decline rate on 2,239 attempts.
The top three BINs together account for 40.3% of all risk declines.

Every other BIN in the top 10 had between 68 and 92 risk declines, with risk-decline rates of 2.4% to 2.6% of attempts. Examples: 922002 (Lotus Bank) 92 declines at 2.4%, 922003 (Lotus Bank) 91 at 2.4%, 912002 (Harbor Bank) 76 at 2.4%.
The three leading BINs have risk-decline rates of 13.3% to 15.7%, roughly five to six times the 2.4%–2.6% rates seen on the other top-10 BINs.

response.headline: Three Harbor Bank BINs (911001, 911003 and 911002) had the most risk declines in 22–31 Oct 2026, together making up 40.3% of the 2,516 card risk declines in the period.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Break down the 911001/911002/911003 declines by decline code (ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE vs RISK_RULE_DECLINE vs SUSPECTED_FRAUD), by day and by merchant, and check whether any risk-rule change or fraud alert coincided with 22 Oct.
hypotheses.rationale: All three top BINs belong to one issuer and share a 911 prefix, and their risk-decline rates are far above the other BINs, so the cause looks specific to this group rather than general volume.
hypotheses.text: Harbor Bank's 911xxx BIN range may be hit by a tighter issuer-side or acquirer-side risk rule, or by a fraud pattern targeting these BINs.

hypotheses.rationale: Attempt volume was up 39% versus usual in this window, so counts rise with volume. However, the high rates on the top three BINs are not explained by volume alone.
hypotheses.text: Part of the volume of risk declines may reflect the sale-period traffic surge rather than a change in risk behaviour.
